opportunities.title: 24/7 intake, triage and booking agent across phone, web form and after-hours emergency
opportunities.problem: All demand lands on one phone number or a web form, with no calendar, chat or after-hours triage tooling, while a single named Office Administrator covers intake and back-office admin for a 118+ community, four-county, three-location operation that also promises 24/7 emergency service. During heat waves and cold snaps the same person is the only gate between a ringing line and a truck, and after hours the gate is an on-call technician who is already working.
evidence: Service requests are taken by phone (732-218-8400) or a website contact form; no calendar/online booking link, and the contact page shows an 'Email' label with no address published -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/contact-us/
The team page lists exactly one Office Administrator handling intake, scheduling and admin for the HQ plus Freehold and Westfield locations -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/team/
24/7 emergency heating and AC service is advertised, with emergency calls prioritized for Woodbridge and nearby towns -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/hvac-service-faqs/
Service footprint is 118+ communities across Middlesex, Union, Monmouth and Somerset counties -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/service-areas/
A Google Ads conversion tag (AW-11398007189) and Site Kit load on every page, so paid leads arrive at a form or a phone with no self-service path -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/
Published testimonial describes an on-call serviceman arriving Saturday night after a long prior shift, i.e. after-hours demand is absorbed by field staff -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/testimonials/

Measured analogue for inbound booking/desk work: generative-AI assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14% across 5,179 support agents, 34% for novice/low-skilled agents (NBER working paper w31161; the brief notes a 2025 QJE version - working paper, treat transfer to a 5-15 person HVAC shop as an inference) -> https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161
opportunities.agent_design: A voice + SMS + web-form agent sits behind the existing 732-218-8400 line (overflow and after-hours first, main line later) and on the Gravity Forms inquiry path. On each contact it runs a structured triage: property type, equipment and fuel (gas, oil, heat pump, boiler), no-heat vs no-cool vs water/refrigerant leak, system age, warranty status, and safety red flags (gas smell, CO alarm, no heat with an infant or elderly occupant). Safety and true-emergency cases are escalated immediately by SMS/voice to the on-call technician with a structured summary; everything else is booked into open slots by town and technician skill, priced from a fixed diagnostic-fee rule, and written back to the dispatch/CRM record with a transcript. It also answers the recurring questions the site already publishes (the $299 maintenance agreement, 15% parts-and-labor discount, PSE&G/Elizabethtown Gas programs, service-area coverage) and captures agreement upsells. Human approval sits at: every safety-flagged dispatch, any quote above the standard diagnostic fee, warranty or goodwill decisions, and a next-morning review queue of low-confidence transcripts.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is not a website chatbot. It has to answer and place real phone calls 24/7, hold a structured diagnostic conversation, respect refrigerant/safety escalation rules, and write jobs into a dispatch system - none of which a subscription chatbot does. It also needs telephony (number provisioning, call recording consent), calendar/skill-based slot logic across three locations, and an auditable transcript trail, with a fallback that never strands a caller. A mis-booked emergency or a missed gas-leak flag is a safety and liability event, not a UX bug.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $14,000-$30,000/year of avoided intake labor, plus an unquantified upside from after-hours and overflow calls that currently go unanswered
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes the agent absorbs 15-25 hours/week of intake and call-back work (inference from one administrator covering three locations and 118+ communities). Priced at NJ median wages: dispatcher $54,590/yr and customer-service rep $47,740/yr = about $23-$26/hour base, about $30-$34/hour loaded at an assumed 1.3x payroll multiplier; 0.2-0.35 FTE displaced. The 14%/34% productivity figures are transferred from a customer-support setting, not measured in HVAC. Recovered-revenue upside is deliberately not quantified: no average ticket or call-volume figure is published for this business, and no NJ lost-call benchmark could be sourced (search providers were rate-limited during this run).

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: triage script built from the company's own FAQ, service-area and financing pages; agent deployed on a dedicated after-hours/overflow number that forwards from the main line, plus a web-form responder; calendar write-back and SMS escalation to the on-call rotation; a daily transcript and exception-review dashboard; measured deflection, booked-job rate, escalation accuracy and average handle time on real calls, with a 1-week shadow mode before it answers live.

opportunities.title: Utility rebate and financing packet agent for install jobs
opportunities.problem: Every qualifying installation drags a second workflow behind it: PSE&G and Elizabethtown Gas on-bill 0% programs up to $25,000 plus Synchrony promotional credit applications, each with its own eligibility rules, forms and document set, all administered by the same single office administrator while the install crew is already on site. Missing or wrong paperwork delays the rebate and the customer's financing, which is exactly where a 'no-surprise pricing' promise gets tested.
evidence: Financing page lists PSE&G and Elizabethtown Gas on-bill 0% programs up to $25,000 plus promotional Synchrony Bank financing, with the company named as a participating contractor in both utility programs -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/hvac-financing/
Badges include a 2024 PSE&G Energy Efficiency Trade Ally award, i.e. rebate-linked work is a marketed part of the offer -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/emergency-hvac-service/
Only one Office Administrator is named for intake, scheduling and back-office admin across three locations -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/team/

Product breadth (full Coleman line plus Fujitsu, Bosch, Nest, oil-to-gas conversions, heat pumps) means equipment-specific rebate eligibility rules apply per job -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/hvac-freehold-nj/

Industry constraint: utility/state program paperwork and refrigerant recordkeeping carry compliance duties, so machine-generated documents need a human sign-off and an audit trail -> https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/49-9021.00
opportunities.agent_design: An agent triggered when an install is quoted or sold: it reads the job record (equipment model, efficiency rating, fuel, address, town), checks eligibility across the PSE&G, Elizabethtown Gas and Synchrony programs against a maintained rules file, and assembles the packet - pre-filled application forms, the document checklist (utility bill, proof of ownership, signed scope), customer-facing instructions, and a status tracker per job. It chases missing documents directly with the customer by SMS/email, flags jobs where the rebate or on-bill amount changes the quoted price, and reconciles the credit when it lands against the invoice and QuickBooks-style accounting. Human approval: the office administrator reviews and signs every submission and is the only party who submits to the utility or lender; any eligibility ambiguity or price change routes to a person before the customer sees it.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is document extraction plus rule evaluation plus form generation across three programs that change their terms, wired into the job record and accounting. Off-the-shelf chatbots cannot read a job record, fill program-specific PDFs, track a claim through to payment, or keep an audit trail. Program rules are effectively compliance rules: an agent that promises a rebate the customer does not qualify for is a consumer-protection problem, so the design needs deterministic eligibility logic and human sign-off, not free-form generation.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $4,000-$15,000/year in avoided administration, plus faster rebate and financing turnaround that shortens cash-collection time on rebate-funded installs
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 0.5-1.5 administrator hours per qualifying install (inference; no time study located) and that 30-50% of installs touch at least one program (inference from the marketing emphasis on financing and the PSE&G trade-ally positioning). If install volume runs 100-250/year, that is 20-190 hours/year at about $30/hour loaded (NJ customer-service rep median $47,740/yr x 1.3). No revenue, install count or rebate dollar volume is published, so the cash-timing benefit is stated qualitatively rather than priced; the 14% support-productivity figure in the brief is a customer-support result and is not applied here.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: eligibility rules file and document checklist built for the two utility programs plus Synchrony; a form-assembly and pre-fill pipeline for the current top three install types; a status tracker board; dry-run on 10-15 closed jobs to measure hours saved and error rate; one program submitted end-to-end with administrator sign-off. No direct submissions to utilities or lenders in the pilot.

opportunities.title: Maintenance-agreement retention and seasonal scheduling agent
opportunities.problem: The $299 maintenance agreement with two annual visits and a 15% parts-and-labor discount, plus a gift-card referral program, generate two seasonal scheduling waves and a continuous renewal-and-tracking workload - and there is no customer portal, so every touch is a manual outbound call, form or text from the one office administrator while emergency intake keeps interrupting her.
evidence: $299 residential maintenance agreement with two annual visits (spring and fall) and 15% off parts and labor for agreement customers -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/hvac-freehold-nj/
A $25 Amazon gift-card referral program creates additional tracking and follow-up work -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/promos/

No customer portal, chat widget or self-service booking was detected on the home or contact pages, so agreement customers have no way to self-schedule their visits -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/contact-us/
Recurring-revenue agreements plus the referral program are flagged as repeat scheduling and tracking work for a one-administrator office spanning three locations -> https://tempcontrolnj.com/team/

NBER working paper w31161: +14% issues resolved per hour with an AI assistant in support work, larger gains for less-experienced staff - the closest measured analogue for repetitive outbound/scheduling desk work (working paper, not an HVAC result) -> https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161

Seasonality is structural in this trade: heating and cooling demand spikes drive overtime and on-call coverage, so the spring/fall agreement waves collide with emergency volume -> https://www.bls.gov/ooh/installation-maintenance-and-repair/heating-air-conditioning-and-refrigeration-mechanics-and-installers.htm
opportunities.agent_design: An agent owns the agreement book: it reads the customer list and last-visit dates, opens the spring and fall scheduling waves, and contacts each customer by SMS/email with two or three offered slots by town cluster and technician route, handling replies, reschedules and opt-outs, and writing confirmed visits into the dispatch calendar. It runs the pre-season renewal sequence with reminders at defined intervals, flags lapsed agreements for a human save call, and promotes the 15% discount and referral program at the right moment in the cycle. It also produces a weekly at-risk list (customers who declined contact, overdue visits, agreements expiring within 60 days) and a per-wave completion dashboard. Human approval: the administrator approves each wave before send, owns all save calls on high-value or commercial accounts, and reviews any reply the agent classifies as a complaint or a price dispute.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: It needs to read the actual agreement and job history, reason over route and town clusters so it does not offer slots that cannot be served, hold a multi-turn reschedule conversation, write back to the calendar, and stay suppressing customers who already booked. A generic email/chatbot subscription has no access to that data and no write path, and bulk-sending blasts from a consumer tool to a few hundred customers at a 15%-discount promise is a brand and TCPA-adjacent risk (consent and opt-out handling must be built in).

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $5,000-$20,000/year, from 8-40 retained or recovered agreements plus 30-90 hours/year of scheduling labor avoided
impact_estimate.assumptions: Agreement count is not published, so 100-300 active agreements is an inference from roughly 1,000 sales/year implied by the 2023 anniversary pledge ($20 per sale against a $20,000 goal - arithmetic on the company's own stated target, not a reported figure). Assumes a 10-15% improvement in renewal/visit completion (inference; no HVAC renewal benchmark could be sourced - search providers were rate-limited in this run), valuing each retained agreement at its $299 fee only, with the 15%-discount repair pull-through left unpriced. Labor priced at the NJ customer-service rep median $47,740/yr x 1.3 loaded, about $30/hour.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: run the next spring-or-fall wave for one town cluster (roughly 30-60 agreements) with automated offer, reschedule and reminder handling; build the at-risk and expiry list; deliver a wave dashboard showing contact rate, booked rate, reschedule rate, declines and hours saved versus a manual control group, plus a renewal sequence ready for the following cycle.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (20/30): the operational signals are unusually concrete and mutually reinforcing for a small contractor - one named office administrator, phone-and-form-only intake, a 24/7 promise with no triage tooling, three locations, 118+ communities, and rebate/financing paperwork in every install - but all of it is company-published, no independent review data (Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi) could be captured, and the pain intensity itself is therefore inferred rather than demonstrated by complaint volumes or missed-call data. Fit (18/20): nearly all of the value sits in capability A with a real D component (forms, calendar, dispatch and accounting write-back); nothing requires hardware or a data-science team. Ability to pay (11/20): growing, multi-location, spends on Google Ads and paid search, qualified as a PSE&G trade ally, and does enough volume to pledge $20,000 to charity, but it is an owner-operated shop with five publicly named staff, no published revenue, and a likely conservative IT budget - a modest, bounded pilot is more sellable than a platform. Ease (10/15): no ServiceTitan/Housecall-style platform was detected, which means no vendor lock but also fresh integration work; the phone line, Gravity Forms and public FAQ content make a 2-4 week pilot feasible. Strategic (13/15): a fully repeatable pattern - the same three agents (intake, rebate packets, agreement waves) resell almost unchanged to HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors across Middlesex and Union counties. Overall 72/100 with moderate confidence: recommend a scope-and-pilot conversation, not a large commitment, and validate call volume and agreement counts in the first meeting since neither is published.

best_evidence_signal: One named Office Administrator handles all phone/form intake and back-office admin for a 118+ community, four-county, three-location operation that advertises 24/7 emergency service, with no online booking or after-hours triage tooling anywhere on the site - https://tempcontrolnj.com/team/ (with https://tempcontrolnj.com/contact-us/)
